AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Pest and Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Pest and Disease Control.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Pest and Disease Control.

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Overgrazing continuously

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Poultry Rearing in a Fold? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Poultry Rearing in a Fold.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Poultry Rearing in a Fold.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Poultry Rearing in a Fold.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Poultry Rearing in a Fold.

4. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

5. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

6. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Conservation Measures? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Conservation Measures.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation Measures.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Conservation Measures.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Conservation Measures.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 0 °C

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Glucose and oxygen
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Preserving animal products and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Cleaning the Kitchen 9 4.0 Production Techniques 4.1 Sewing Skills: Constructing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Pest and Disease Control.

2. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

3. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Poultry Rearing in a Fold.

4. C — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

5. C — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

6. D — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Conservation Measures.

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygiene Practices 3.1 Cleaning the Kit.

9. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

10. A — 100 °C

11. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preserving Animal Products 9 2.6 Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal 11 3.0 Hygie.

12. A — Glucose and oxygen

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Cooking: Preparing a Balanced Meal; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
